text: {"features":[{"evidence":"recurring misspellings","name":"Writing polish","description":"This captures how cleanly the letter is written at the sentence level, especially whether spelling and typographical errors distract from the applicant's credibility.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Frequent spelling or typing errors materially distract from the content and make the letter feel careless."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Noticeable errors appear more than once, but the letter remains readable overall."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Only minor or isolated slips appear; the letter is generally polished."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter is clean, professional, and free of distracting copy errors."}]},{"evidence":"7 years ... launched 6 production services","name":"Production track record","description":"This captures how much real production software experience the letter conveys through years of work, service ownership, testing, maintenance, launches, and operating responsibility.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Shows only minimal professional scope, such as early-career experience with limited production ownership or few launches."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Shows solid early-career production experience with some meaningful maintenance or launch work."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Shows substantial multi-year ownership across several production services."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Shows extensive production history with repeated testing, maintenance, launches, and clear operational responsibility."}]},{"evidence":"Doctoral degree in computer science","name":"Advanced academic qualification","description":"This captures how strongly the applicant's formal academic background matches or exceeds the posting's preference for graduate-level technical study.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Bachelor's degree or equivalent only; meets the minimum but does not add a preferred graduate credential."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Master's degree or comparable advanced graduate study in a relevant technical field."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Doctoral degree or similarly research-intensive advanced qualification in a relevant technical field."}]},{"evidence":"building software that makes secure development the default","name":"Role-specific motivation","description":"This captures how clearly the letter explains why this particular security engineering role is the applicant's target, rather than just another software position.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Interest is generic and could apply to many backend or software roles."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Mentions security or Google, but the connection to this team's actual work remains broad."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Clearly explains attraction to secure-development tooling, vulnerability response, or lifecycle security work."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Gives a persuasive, role-specific rationale tied closely to the team's mandate and the applicant's own trajectory."}]},{"evidence":"improvements there are inherited by every team downstream","name":"Foundational platform orientation","description":"This captures whether the applicant values building central infrastructure whose benefits compound across many teams rather than staying local to one product surface.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"No meaningful platform or cross-team perspective is expressed."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Shows generic excitement about scale without explaining a platform mindset."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Explicitly values central infrastructure, foundational tooling, or organization-wide systems."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Clearly articulates the multiplier effect of foundational systems across downstream teams, products, or the broader engineering ecosystem."}]},{"evidence":"make the secure path the easy path","name":"Developer enablement mindset","description":"This captures whether the letter frames security work as helping other engineers succeed through usable defaults and lower-friction tooling.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Does not show much empathy for downstream developers or users of the tooling."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Briefly suggests helping developers, but without a clear enablement angle."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Explicitly values making secure behavior easier for product engineers."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Strongly frames the work as proactive developer enablement that reduces friction while improving security outcomes."}]},{"evidence":"scale scarce security judgment across an entire company","name":"Automation leverage framing","description":"This captures whether the applicant understands the role as a leverage problem in which tooling multiplies limited security expertise and reduces manual toil.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Does not frame the work in leverage, capacity, or automation terms."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Says automation matters, but not why it changes the security function."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Explains automation as a way to reduce manual workload or streamline triage."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Frames automation as a multiplier of scarce security expertise, variant analysis capacity, or company-wide defensive reach."}]},{"evidence":"quiet, dependable systems are my favorite thing to build","name":"Reliability mindset","description":"This captures whether the applicant signals a genuine preference for dependable infrastructure, maintenance discipline, and high standards in systems that protect other systems.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"No clear value signal about dependability, maintenance, or standards."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Makes general statements about quality or correctness."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Shows a clear preference for dependable infrastructure, maintainer habits, or high standards."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Presents a strong, consistent orientation toward quiet resilience, maintainership, or building security tooling to a higher bar."}]},{"evidence":"Python became my workhorse","name":"Python depth","description":"This captures how concretely the letter presents Python as a meaningful production language for services, tooling, automation, or analysis.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Provides no meaningful Python evidence."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Mentions Python use in passing, without showing depth or scope."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Describes regular Python use for services, automation, analysis, or internal tooling."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Presents Python as a strong production language with evidence such as typed or tested services, central tooling, or major automation layers."}]},{"evidence":"Python agents ... Go services constrain every step","name":"Agentic architecture","description":"This captures whether the applicant shows real design ownership of agent-based systems rather than merely naming agents as a buzzword.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"No agentic or agent-based system work is described."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Mentions agents at a high level, but without architecture or implementation detail."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Describes building agentic tooling with Python agents and Go back-end control."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Explains concrete architectural boundaries such as permissions, constraints, auditability, task decomposition, or supervision."}]},{"evidence":"evaluation practices required to operate them","name":"AI production maturity","description":"This captures whether the applicant has only touched AI superficially or has shipped model-backed systems with production-minded caution and controls.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"No meaningful AI experience is presented."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Mentions AI interest or limited experimentation without production scope."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Describes shipping model-backed or LLM-based functionality in production."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Shows production maturity through evaluation, guardrails, failure-mode handling, or explicit concern for trustworthiness."}]},{"evidence":"threat modeling and code review","name":"Security assessment practice","description":"This captures whether the applicant has actually performed security reviews and assessments, and how hands-on or rigorous that work appears.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"No security review or assessment work is described."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Provides only general or passive mention of security exposure."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Shows clear hands-on assessment work such as threat modeling, code review, attack-surface analysis, or release-cycle reviews."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Shows repeated or formal assessment practice with remediation follow-through and an attack-minded perspective."}]},{"evidence":"classified, deduplicated, and routed","name":"Vulnerability automation","description":"This captures whether the letter shows direct experience building tooling for vulnerability intake, triage, ownership, or response workflows.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"No vulnerability-handling automation is described."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Mentions security automation vaguely, without clear triage or workflow details."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Shows clear experience building intake, triage, routing, or queue-handling automation for vulnerability reports."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Provides rich operational detail such as classification, deduplication, prioritization, ownership mapping, or measurable reduction of manual work."}]},{"evidence":"proper graph algorithms","name":"Algorithmic fluency","description":"This captures whether the letter demonstrates substantive command of algorithms or data structures through concrete problem-solving examples.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Gives no evidence beyond generic technical competence."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Claims strength in algorithms or data structures without a concrete example."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Provides a specific example of an algorithmic redesign or better structure choice improving a system."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Shows especially strong fluency through nontrivial examples such as graph work, streaming computation, hot-path redesign, matching, or large-scale deduplication."}]},{"evidence":"OSCP certification","name":"Offensive security validation","description":"This captures the strength of external or practice-based evidence that the applicant actively develops offensive security instincts.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"No external signal of offensive security practice is provided."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Shows an entry-level signal such as Security+ or occasional CTF participation."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Shows a strong signal such as OSCP or sustained serious CTF participation."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Shows multiple strong signals or unusually credible hands-on proof, such as OSCP plus top CTF finishes."}]},{"evidence":"maintain an open-source project","name":"Open-source stewardship","description":"This captures whether the applicant goes beyond private work to contribute to or maintain software used by others.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"No open-source contribution or maintenance is mentioned."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Mentions occasional upstream patches or a lightly maintained small project."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Shows ongoing contribution or maintenance responsibility for a project others use."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Shows clear stewardship of an actively used project or library, including reviews, releases, roadmap ownership, or community interaction."}]},{"evidence":"distributed task queue with exactly-once semantics","name":"Personal systems initiative","description":"This captures the ambition and technical depth of self-directed projects used to stretch beyond day-job requirements.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"No personal build is mentioned, or only very trivial side activity appears."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Mentions a small utility or practice project with modest technical depth."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Shows a substantial self-directed build that required meaningful system design effort."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Shows an ambitious systems project involving distributed systems, replication, consensus, fault tolerance, recovery, or similarly hard engineering problems."}]},{"evidence":"measured its worth in the hours of expert attention it returned","name":"Specificity of evidence","description":"This captures how often the letter backs claims with concrete mechanisms, constraints, or outcomes instead of relying on generic assertions.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Mostly makes abstract claims of skill or interest without concrete proof."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Names relevant tasks or domains, but examples remain generic or list-like."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Backs multiple claims with concrete examples, mechanisms, or scopes."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Consistently gives precise evidence showing how the work functioned, what constraints mattered, or what changed as a result."}]}]}
